title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 214 (Security for payment of costs and expenses of investigation)

content.overview: Section 214 provides that where an investigation is ordered by the Central Government under section 210 on an application made by members under section 213, the Central Government may, before appointing an inspector, require the applicants to give security for such amount as it may specify for payment of costs and expenses of the investigation.
content.glance: Investigation ordered on members’ application (s. 213 → s. 210 path): CG may require applicants to give security for costs and expenses before appointing an inspector; does not apply to CG’s own-motion public-interest investigations.
content.study: Where an investigation is ordered by the Central Government under section 210 on an application made by members under section 213, the Central Government may before appointing an inspector under section 210, require the applicant to give such security for payment of costs and expenses of investigation as it may specify. Current-law framing: confirm the investigation was ordered on a members’ application under s. 213; note CG’s power to require security before appointing an inspector; distinguish from investigations ordered of the Government’s own motion in public interest under s. 210, where this security condition does not apply.

sections.heading: Scope
sections.body: Applies where investigation is ordered under s. 210 on a members’ application under s. 213.

sections.heading: Security
sections.body: Central Government may require applicants to give security for costs and expenses of the investigation before appointing an inspector.

sections.heading: Exclusion
sections.body: Does not apply to investigations the Central Government orders of its own motion (e.g. public interest under s. 210).

provisions.title: Security for payment of costs and expenses of investigation

examples.title: Security before inspector appointment
examples.body: Members obtain a Tribunal order under s. 213 and the Central Government is to appoint inspectors under s. 210. Before appointment, CG may require those applicants to furnish security for investigation costs under s. 214.

examples.title: Public-interest investigation
examples.body: CG orders investigation in public interest under s. 210 without any members’ application. Section 214 security does not apply.

hypotheticals.question: Must every investigation under Chapter XIV be preceded by security from applicants?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 214 applies only where investigation is ordered on a members’ application under s. 213. Own-motion and other non-applicant-triggered investigations are outside this security requirement.

distinctions.title: Security for costs (s. 214) vs Tribunal-ordered investigation (s. 213)
distinctions.left: CG may require applicants to secure costs before appointing inspector
distinctions.right: Tribunal gateway for members to seek investigation order

misconceptions.trap: Security under s. 214 is required for every SFIO or public-interest investigation.
misconceptions.correction: Section 214 is limited to investigations ordered on members’ applications under s. 213. It does not apply to CG own-motion or SFIO assignment routes as such.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 214 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm members’ application path (s. 213 → s. 210). II. Note CG power to require security before inspector appointment. III. Exclude own-motion cases. IV. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Application path; security demand; precise relief.
